_revision: draft r2, 2026-09-24 (fix round 1): request->release wall clock with work throughput kept separate; footprint bytes separate from traversed bytes; evaluator must be frozen for correctness; modeled lower bound when release is unknown; attempts carry layer=delivered and one of three methods
_about: One record per run: one seat lease executing one Knot (or one campaign arm). Field groups follow research-2026-09/SYNTHESIS.md 'The unit: one run, not one token' plus the Correction (traversal group). Type words: string, number, integer, boolean, object, array, iso8601 (UTC 'Z' timestamp string), sha256 (64 hex), any. 'nullable': true means null is allowed BUT the group's null_reasons must then name the field. Validation is done by ledger_validate.py (stdlib), not by a jsonschema library.

identity._doc: Who ran what where. Everything the comparison engine pins (identity.json) is repeated here so a ledger line stands alone.

knot_id.doc: Knot this run executed (knot_lifecycle.py); null for pre-Knot runs

model.doc: revision = git sha; bytes = checkpoint bytes (the footprint)

runtime.doc: image digest pinned; engine = vllm | llama.cpp | ...; Run 3 adds attention_backend / linear_kernel from serve.log

prereg.doc: commit null when the prereg was not committed before data (say so in notes)

clocks._doc: The buyer's clock starts at the capacity request and stops at confirmed release. All UTC ISO-8601. Each clock may carry a 'sources' entry naming where it came from and its precision.

t_request.doc: capacity requested (create clicked / API call / TUI provision)

t_work_start.doc: first recorded unit of work started

t_work_end.doc: last recorded unit of work finished

t_released.doc: provider confirmed the seat was deleted / released (container stop is NOT release)

rules: non-null clocks must be non-decreasing in the order listed

acquisition._doc: The denominator. Every provisioning attempt for this run, including failures. A listing is not an attempt: attempts carry layer 'delivered' and method api-create | console-create | tui-provision.
rules: every attempt: layer == delivered and method in {api-create, console-create, tui-provision}

work._doc: attempted / completed / correct / accepted / lost / restarts. correct means a FROZEN evaluator passed, not HTTP 200. accepted = correct AND within the latency gate (when no evaluator exists, accepted = completed AND within gate, and correct is null with a reason).

evaluator.doc: frozen must be true and ref non-empty (criterion id / sidecar sha) for correct to be non-null

lost.doc: sent and never answered (timeout, connection reset, interrupted)

restarts.doc: engine or seat restarts during the work window

cells.doc: optional per-cell breakdown for benchmark-style runs

rules: correct non-null requires evaluator.frozen == true and non-empty evaluator.ref

sustained._doc: A recorded window in 5-minute buckets: minimum, median, and last quarter / first quarter of accepted per bucket. required_window_s is 3600 (Fable) or 7200 (Astra); meets_required_window says whether this run's window is long enough AND uninterrupted.
rules: meets_required_window == (window_s >= required_window_s and not interrupted and work.accepted is non-null) when window_s non-null; an ungraded window never qualifies

traversal._doc: SYNTHESIS Correction: every decode step is one weight traversal. footprint_bytes is what is RESIDENT (allocated); bytes_per_traversal is what is TRAVERSED per step, which for MoE is the active subset and stays null unless measured. Each numeric field carries a sibling '<field>_basis' saying measured | estimated | null and how.

footprint_bytes.doc: resident weight bytes (model buffers); NOT traversed bytes

bytes_per_traversal.doc: bytes actually read per decode step; null unless measured

rules: accepted_closures_per_traversal == work.accepted / traversals (rel 1e-3) when traversals and accepted are non-null
footprint_bytes and bytes_per_traversal may not be silently equal for MoE models: the basis must say measured if they are

money._doc: Modeled = list rate x minutes over the buyer's window (request -> release). When release is unknown, modeled_usd is null and modeled_lower_bound_usd carries request -> work_end (or the widest known window) with its basis. Billed = the invoice line when it posts. Credits are separate and never netted. Energy is for estate seats (metered watts x hours x tariff).

modeled_minutes.doc: (t_released - t_request) / 60; null unless both clocks exist

modeled_lower_bound_basis.doc: which clocks bound the lower-bound window

credits_usd.doc: credit consumed, as the provider reports it

energy.doc: all nullable inside; meter names the instrument or null

rules: modeled_usd non-null requires t_request and t_released non-null and modeled_minutes == (t_released - t_request)/60 (tolerance 0.02 min)

derived._doc: Cost per accepted unit and wall clock per accepted unit. wall_s_per_accepted is the BUYER'S clock (t_request -> t_released) / accepted, null with a reason when either clock is unknown. Work-time throughput is kept separately and never substitutes for it.
rules: wall_s_per_accepted == (t_released - t_request) / accepted when non-null; must be null when either clock is null
work_s_per_accepted == work window / accepted; accepted_per_work_s == accepted / work window

receipts._doc: References to the retained bytes. Paths are repo-relative or absolute; sha256 when the file is content-addressed (MANIFEST.sha256); sha256_verified says whether the builder recomputed and matched it.

items.doc: kind in {cell, env, env_normalized, image, manifest, log, serve_log, engine_output, evaluation, clocks, arm_summary, arm_file, replay, grade, smoke, availability, invoice, prereg, event_log, meter, closure, file}

manifest_verified.doc: true when every MANIFEST line was recomputed and matched

null_reasons_rule: Every group is an object that may carry 'null_reasons': {field: reason}. Every field in that group whose value is null MUST have a non-empty reason there. Reasons are prose, e.g. 'Run 1 did not record droplet deletion time'.
